why.text: Loose volcanic soils on Etna's slopes at 300 to 1,100 m, with big day-night temperature swings and much more rain than the rest of Sicily.

styles.text: Dry white, red and rosato, plus white and rosé sparkling wine; the red also comes as riserva.

climate.text: Temperate Mediterranean; wettest in autumn and winter, driest in June and July. Rain averages about 600 mm on the south-west side and up to 1,200 mm on the north and north-east.

soil.text: Volcanic ash, sand, lapilli and pumice; 80% of vineyards sit on volcanic soils that are loose, stony and well drained. The other 20% are alluvial soils and vertisols.

altitude.text: Vines mostly grow between 300 and 900 m, and reach up to 1,100 m.

tastes.text: White: straw yellow, delicate, dry and fresh. Red: ruby, garnet with age, intense, dry, warm and full. Rosato: dry, more or less intense pink. Sparkling: fine, lasting bubbles, sometimes citrus or floral notes.

styles.name: Etna bianco superiore
styles.text: White from Milo grapes only, at least 80% Carricante.

styles.name: Etna rosso riserva
styles.text: Red aged at least four years, 12 months in wood, inside the zone.

styles.name: Etna spumante
styles.text: Bottle-fermented only, at least 18 months on the lees; white or rosé.

why.text: Mostly limestone with terra rossa in a hot, arid Mediterranean climate with strong summer day-night swings, and a blend unique here: Nero d'Avola with Frappato.

styles.text: Dry still reds only: Cerasuolo di Vittoria and the Classico, released later.

climate.text: Hot, arid Mediterranean climate with little summer rain. Mean annual temperature runs from 15.4 °C (high hills) to 19.6 °C (coast). July-August day-night swing is 9 to 14 °C. Annual rain is 385 to 499 mm.

soil.text: Mostly limestone: Miocene calcarenites under loose Pleistocene soils, with some sandy and clay-sandy areas. About half is leached brown soil with terra rossa.

altitude.text: Coast 0 to 200 m, mid hills 200 to 350 m, high hills above 350 m.

tastes.text: Cerasuolo di Vittoria: cherry red to violet, floral to fruity, dry, full, soft. Classico: cherry to garnet, cherry notes, with age dried plum, chocolate, leather, tobacco.

styles.name: Cerasuolo di Vittoria
styles.text: 50 to 70% Nero d'Avola, 30 to 50% Frappato; sold from 1 June after harvest.

styles.name: Cerasuolo di Vittoria Classico
styles.text: Same blend; sold only from 31 March of the second year after harvest.

why.text: Sandy granite soils, mild winters, constant sun and salty wind in northern Sardinia give aromatic, mineral Vermentino with good natural acidity.

styles.text: Dry to off-dry still white, plus frizzante, spumante, passito and late-harvest versions.

climate.text: Warm temperate with mild winters. Rain falls in autumn and winter, under 700 mm a year, and a constant wind blows, particularly salty near the sea.

soil.text: Mainly granite, covered by coarse sand mixed at times with clay. Sandy, stony soils are generally best, and the soils are high in potassium.

altitude.text: Vineyards must stand no higher than 500 m above sea level.

tastes.text: Pale straw with greenish glints, intense pleasant aroma, dry to off-dry, sometimes slightly bitter finish. Wood-aged wines are more intense, with light vanilla.

styles.name: Superiore
styles.text: Lower yield of 9 t/ha, at least 13% alcohol.

styles.name: Passito
styles.text: Grapes dried to 15% potential alcohol; golden, full and aromatic; sold from 1 May.

styles.name: Vendemmia tardiva
styles.text: Late harvest, at least 13% alcohol, sold from 15 January.

styles.name: Spumante
styles.text: Metodo classico needs at least nine months on lees; first disgorgement date on label.
